title: Scalable, High-Fidelity Monitoring of Application Communication Patterns in Vernier
problem: Understanding irregular, dynamic HPC application communication patterns at scale is critical for optimization and architecture evaluation. Current approaches are either too coarse (aggregated statistics) or too detailed (exhaustive traces), creating scalability and flexibility trade-offs.
motivation: System architects and software optimizers need targeted, scalable communication pattern data for specific annotated regions, not generic application-wide traces or aggregates.
method: The Vernier system monitors application communication using histograms—buckets that count message frequencies in different categories—rather than recording every individual message. You annotate points in your code where communication happens, and Vernier collects statistical summaries for each annotated region. This approach is fast enough to run during actual execution (online) or afterward from logs (offline), and the compact statistics can feed directly into benchmarking and network simulations.
key_novelty: Vernier uses statistical histograms to track application communication patterns instead of detailed message traces, making monitoring fast enough to run during execution and scalable enough for network simulation and optimization.
contributions: Vernier system for scalable communication monitoring
Histogram-based statistical approach to communication characterization
Configurable per-annotation collection enabling targeted data gathering
Demonstration on production HPC applications at scale

metrics.accuracy: Statistically accurate representation of communication patterns

limitations: Abstract-only analysis; specific application cases not detailed; accuracy vs. trace completeness trade-off not quantified; simulation validation not mentioned
